summary: Field Shift is an interactive geospatial decision support platform that helps farmers look at climate resilient crop rotations using NASA Earth observations. It was built for all 99 counties in Iowa, so we integrated historical temperature, precipitation, and solar radiation data from NASA POWER with county level agricultural scenario models. Users can interact with a map, compare four crop rotation strategies (conventional corn soybean, clover, cereal rye, and perennial systems), and customize the importance of water quality, soil health, and profitability. A transparent scoring system gives trade offs, while adjustable economic guardrails gives strategies that may be financially unsuitable. The platform combines geographic visualization, climate data, and scenario comparisons to make agricultural planning more accessible and explainable. Instead of just recommending a universal crop rotation, Field Shift shows how NASA data can inform location specific decisions that balance environmental sustainability with economic viability. Field Shift is a decision support prototype, and its modeled scenario outputs are intended for exploration instead of field validated agricultural prescriptions.
details:
Field Shift:

The Problem

Agricultural productivity increasingly depends on farmers' ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions. Rising temperatures, unpredictable precipitation, water scarcity, and soil degradation create challenges for traditional farming systems.

In Iowa, where corn soybean rotations dominate much of the agricultural landscape, farmers must be able to balance crop productivity, water conservation, soil health, and profitability. But the information needed to compare agricultural strategies is often distributed across different datasets and difficult to understand.

Our Solution

Field Shift is an interactive, web based geospatial decision-support prototype covering all 99 Iowa counties. It brings NASA climate observations, agricultural scenario estimates, and customizable decision priorities into a single dashboard.

The platform allows users to:

  1. Explore county level conditions: Interact with a choropleth map displaying sustainability scores, corn yield, water quality, soil health, and estimated net returns.
  2. Compare four crop rotation scenarios: Evaluate conventional corn soybean rotation (R0), clover integration (R1), cereal rye cover cropping (R2), and diversified perennial systems (R3).
  3. Access NASA climate information: Retrieve historical temperature, precipitation, and solar radiation records from NASA POWER for selected counties.
  4. Customize priorities: Adjust the relative importance of water quality, soil health, and profitability using interactive sliders.
  5. Apply financial constraints: Set an acceptable profit loss threshold. Scenarios exceeding that threshold relative to the conventional baseline are flagged and excluded from the best fit recommendation.
  6. Interpret recommendations: Review comparative scenario scores, county rankings, radar charts, and supporting climate information.

NASA Earth Observation Integration

Field Shift uses NASA's Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) API to access historical climate information from 2016 through 2025.

The integration includes three environmental variables:

  • T2M: Air temperature at two meters above the surface.
  • PRECTOTCORR: Corrected precipitation.
  • ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN: All-sky surface shortwave solar irradiance.

The application requests data using county centroid coordinates, processes the returned climate time series, and uses server side caching with a 24 hour duration to reduce repeated requests.

This integration makes NASA's climate observations more accessible within a local agricultural decision support interface.

Decision-Support Methodology

Field Shift uses a transparent, weighted scoring approach to compare alternative agricultural scenarios.

Users specify the relative importance of water quality, soil health, and economic performance. The platform combines modeled scenario indicators according to those priorities and applies an economic guardrail before identifying the best fitting alternative.

This approach makes trade offs explicit instead of treating a single agricultural strategy as optimal under every condition. Users can change their priorities and examine how rankings respond.

The current prototype includes illustrative agricultural scenario outputs. These are not independently validated predictions of future crop yields, soil conditions, or farm income.

Technology and Implementation

We used the following technology stack:

  • Next.js and React: Application framework and interactive user interface.
  • TypeScript: Application logic and structured data processing.
  • Tailwind CSS: Responsive dashboard styling.
  • MapLibre GL: Interactive geographic visualization.
  • Recharts: Climate charts, scenario comparisons, and analytical visualizations.
  • NASA POWER API: Historical meteorological and solar radiation data.
  • Vercel: Public deployment and hosting.

Innovation and Creativity

Field Shift combines spatial analysis, NASA Earth observations, customizable sustainability priorities, and economic constraints in one interactive experience.

A central feature is its explainable decision process. Instead of creating an unexplained recommendation, the system allows users to inspect the relative importance of environmental and economic objectives, compare competing scenarios, and examine how different priorities affect the outcome.

The use of county level visualization makes geographically varying conditions easier to explore. Its modular approach also gives it a foundation for incorporating more detailed soil, crop, and climate information.

Intended Impact and Future Development

Field Shift aims to make climate aware agricultural planning more understandable and accessible to farmers, agricultural educators, researchers, and local decision makers.

Potential benefits include improved awareness of climate variability, clearer comparisons between crop rotation options, and more transparent consideration of environmental and economic trade offs.

Future development could incorporate field level soil measurements, additional NASA remote sensing products, locally calibrated crop models, uncertainty estimates, and validation against observed agricultural outcomes.

Our long term vision is a scalable agricultural decision support system that turns Earth observations into practical insights and is still able to keep the role of farmers and agricultural experts in making final management decisions.
